## Project instructions (AGENTS.md — workbench default)

# AGENTS.md — workbench default

> Instructions for any agent working through the Ember Workbench. This is the
> **fallback**: a workspace with its own `AGENTS.md` at its root overrides this
> file entirely. Put project-specific rules there, not here.
>
> Keep this short. It is re-sent on every turn and competes with the work for
> context. Truncated at 8,000 chars.

## Before you touch anything

1. **Read before you write.** Never edit a file you have not read this session.
   Never claim an action you did not take — the operator sees your report, not
   your tools.
2. **Look for the project's own rules.** If the workspace has `AGENTS.md`,
   `CLAUDE.md`, or a `README.md` with conventions, they outrank this file.
3. **Check for a skill.** `use_skill` lists what is available. A stored
   procedure beats improvising, and router skills route to sub-files — load
   those with `use_skill name="..." file="..."`.

## While you work

- **Small steps, but finish.** One logical action at a time, and keep going
  until the task is actually done. Stopping at the first plausible-looking
  result is the most common failure here.
- **Minimal diffs.** `edit_file` over `write_file`; match the surrounding code's
  style, naming, and comment density rather than importing your own.
- **Commands need approval** unless the session is in Auto mode. If one is
  denied, change the approach — do not retry the identical call.
- **Long output is clipped in the middle**, keeping the head and the tail.
  Build errors live in the tail; read it.

## Dependencies — do not churn them

**Do not edit `package.json` (or the equivalent manifest) to change versions
that are already there.** Pinned versions are pinned deliberately: someone chose
them, and a toolchain that shifts under a project turns every later result into
a comparison of library versions rather than of the work.

The single exception: if the task genuinely needs a package that is **not
listed**, add that package. Add it — do not rewrite the versions of the ones
around it.

- If a lockfile exists, install with `npm ci`, not `npm install`. `ci` installs
  exactly what the lockfile says; `install` is free to resolve something newer
  and silently rewrite the lockfile.
- If a pinned version genuinely blocks the task, **say so and stop**. Do not
  downgrade your way around it. That is a decision for the operator, and it is
  usually a sign the real problem is elsewhere.
- Never delete or regenerate a lockfile to make an error go away.

## Before you say you are done

- **Run it.** If what you built can be built, tested, or opened, do that. Read
  the output. Fix what breaks. Repeat until it is clean.
- **Never report completion on code you have not executed.** If you could not
  run it, say so plainly and say why — that is a fine answer; a false "done"
  is not.
- **Report what changed and what you verified.** No preamble, no flattery, no
  summary of how hard the task was.

## Memory

Use `remember` when something is worth carrying past this turn:

- `lesson` — something that cost you time and would cost the next agent time
  (a build quirk, a wrong assumption, an API that does not behave as documented).
- `decision` — a choice made and its reason, so it is not silently relitigated.

Memory is per-workspace and is injected into future sessions on this workspace.
Record the *finding*, not the narration. One line each.

## The working method — CRAFT.md

`CRAFT.md` at the workbench root is the long-form method: how to read what is
actually being asked, how to split a problem along verification seams, how to
know when you are guessing. It is **not** injected by default — roughly 4k
tokens on every turn.

Set `EMBER_CRAFT=on` to load it into the system prompt when the work is hard,
unfamiliar, or high-stakes enough to be worth the budget.

The shipped copy is deliberately generic. If you keep your own working-method
document — one that names your projects, your conventions, and the specific
mistakes that have actually cost you time — point `EMBER_CRAFT_PATH` at it
instead. A method doc is worth more when its examples are yours.

## Honesty rules

- Say "I do not know" rather than producing a confident guess.
- Distinguish what you verified from what you assume. Mark assumptions.
- If a constraint blocks the literal request, say so **before** substituting
  something else — not in the delivery summary.
- Surface bad news early. A problem reported at step two is cheap; the same
  problem discovered at step ten is not.

---

## Environment

- **Platform:** Windows (win32)
- **Workspace root:** `C:/Data/AI/Projects/LMStudioComparison/Results/_SpaceInvaders-qwen3.8-27b-2026-09-06/local`  — every path you pass to a file tool is relative to this, and paths outside it are rejected.
- **run_command shell:** git-bash — POSIX sh, *not* cmd.exe or PowerShell. use Unix syntax (`ls`, `rm`, `cat`, `grep`, `/dev/null`, forward slashes, `$VAR`, `&&`). cmd.exe builtins are NOT available and fail in confusing ways: `dir`, `type`, `findstr`, `%VAR%`, and especially `2>nul`, which silently creates a FILE named `nul` instead of discarding output — write `2>/dev/null`.
- **Working directory does not persist** between commands. Each one starts at the workspace root.

---

## This session: coding agent

You operate on files inside one workspace via tools.
Rules, in order:
1. Never invent file contents — read before you edit. Never claim an action you did not take.
2. Plan briefly (one or two sentences), then act with tools. Work in small steps, but keep going until the task is actually done — do not stop at the first plausible-looking result.
3. Prefer minimal diffs via edit_file; write_file only for new files. Match the existing code style and document public APIs the way the surrounding code does.
4. Writes and commands need user approval; if denied, adjust your approach rather than retrying the same call.
5. Verify your own work before reporting it done. If what you built can be run — a build, a test suite, a page — run it, read the output, and fix what breaks. Never report completion on code you have not executed. If you could not run it, say so plainly and say why.
6. Be terse. Report what changed and what you verified, not how hard you worked. No flattery, no filler.

Skills — stored procedures under .claude/skills in this workspace. When a task matches one, call use_skill with its name BEFORE improvising, then follow the returned instructions:

[Earlier turns were compacted to save context. Summary of the work so far:]

**HAND-OFF NOTE — AAA Retro-Futurism Three.js Arcade / Space Invaders**

**Mission**
Build a Vite + vanilla JS + ES Modules Three.js arcade with 14 retro games, starting with `Space_Invaders/`. Strict constraints:
- No external game engines/physics libs; hand-written collision/physics.
- 100% procedural assets: no `.gltf`, images, audio files.
- Gameplay meshes use `MeshStandardMaterial` PBR.
- Glassmorphism HTML/CSS HUD.
- Unified keyboard + Gamepad input.
- Object pooling, hard 500-particle cap, `InstancedMesh` where useful, explicit `.dispose()`.
- Mandatory `EffectComposer` + `UnrealBloomPass`.
- Required VFX: trauma camera shake, particle bursts, hit-stop, motion trails, shockwave rings, floating score text.
- Workflow: Step 1 init → user says `Begin [Game]` → Step 2 `plan.md` → user says `Plan approved` → Step 3 full implementation, no placeholders. If truncated, stop and resume exactly on `continue`.

**Current state**
- `Space_Invaders` plan is approved.
- Shared core utilities are implemented and mostly verified.
- No `Space_Invaders/` game code has been written yet.
- Next work is full implementation of the approved `Space_Invaders/plan.md`.

**Environment / stack decisions**
- Pinned: `three@0.185.1`, `vite@8.2.2`.
- Vite multi-entry setup.
- `openai-game-studio` / `three-webgl-game` skill was loaded, but its GLB/Rapier defaults are overridden by the mission: vanilla JS, procedural assets, hand-written physics.
- Dependency rule: game code may import `shared/*`; shared code must not import game code; no cross-game imports; relative imports only.

**Key approved Space Invaders design**
- 2D gameplay plane at `z = 0`, camera at `(0, 0, 14)`.
- Player moves laterally, `x ∈ [-7, 7]`, exponential smoothing.
- Invader formation: 11 columns × 5 rows = 55 invaders.
- Species: squid, crab, octopus; values 30/20/10.
- Formation marches, drops on edge, accelerates as invaders die.
- Invaders fire stochastically from bottom-most alive per column.
- Player fire: one active bullet classic rule, small pool headroom.
- AABB collision only.
- Shields: 4 erodible bunkers using instanced blocks.
- UFO mystery ship: high-value, periodic, distinctive VFX/audio.
- Combo multiplier, wave scaling, high score via `localStorage`.
- VFX mapping:
  - Invader kill: shake 0.15, hit-stop 60ms @ 0.15, 30 particles, 1 shockwave, floating score.
  - Player hit: shake 0.45, hit-stop 120ms @ 0.05, 50 particles, 2 shockwaves.
  - UFO kill: shake 0.30, hit-stop 80ms @ 0.10, 60 particles, 2 shockwaves, trail.
  - Wave clear: shake 0.20, 80 particles, 3 shockwaves.

**Bugs found and fixed**
- `FloatingText`: all sprites initially shared one texture, causing text overwrites. Fixed by giving each sprite its own texture.
- `ParticleManager`: `_grav` was lazily initialized but used before `update()`, losing per-particle gravity. Fixed by initializing in constructor.
- `ParticleManager`: `_burstColor` was referenced but not declared. Fixed.
- `ParticleManager`: `burst()` and `update()` shared a temporary color object, causing color corruption when spawning mid-frame. Fixed by giving `burst()` its own temporary color object.
- `ParticleManager`: slot-finding optimized with a rotating cursor to reduce allocation/scan cost.

**Verified shared APIs to use**
- `Engine.js`: `createEngine(canvas, opts)`; `opts.onFrame(dt, elapsed)`; owns renderer/scene/camera/resize/dispose.
- `Input.js`: `new Input()`; call `update()`; read `axisX`, `axisY`, `fire`, `pause`, etc.
- `ObjectPool.js`: `new ObjectPool(factory, size, reset)`; `acquire()`, `release(obj)`, active/free counts.
- `ParticleManager.js`: `new ParticleManager(scene, {cap, size, gravity})`; hard cap 500; `burst(...)`, `update(dt)`, `dispose()`.
- `CameraShake.js`: `new CameraShake({maxOffset, decay})`; `addTrauma(amount)`, `update(dt)`, `apply(camera)`.
- `HitStop.js`: `new HitStop()`; `trigger(duration, timescale)`, `scale(rawDt)`.
- `Shockwave.js`: `new Shockwave(scene)`; pooled rings; `spawn(origin, maxRadius, color)`, `update(dt)`, `dispose()`.
- `MotionTrail.js`: attach to fast movers; `update(dt)`, `dispose()`.
- `FloatingText.js`: `spawn(text, worldPos, color)`, `update(dt)`, `dispose()`.
- `AudioEngine.js`: Web Audio synth; `playSfx(name)`, `startMusic(pattern)`, `setMuted(bool)`, `dispose()`.
- `PostFX.js`: `createPostFX(renderer, scene, camera)`, `resize()`, `dispose()`.
- `NeonMaterials.js`: PBR `MeshStandardMaterial` factory/presets.
- `GlassHUD.js`: DOM glassmorphism HUD; score/lives/overlay/dispose.

**Known implementation nuance**
- `Shockwave.js` uses additive `MeshBasicMaterial` for rings. This is a VFX/presentation exception already in code; gameplay entities should still use `MeshStandardMaterial`.

**Immediate next step**
Implement all approved `Space_Invaders/` files fully, no placeholders. Start with:
1. `Space_Invaders/index.html`
2. `Space_Invaders/config.js`
3. `Space_Invaders/entities/*`
4. `Space_Invaders/systems/*`
5. `Space_Invaders/vfx/*`
6. `Space_Invaders/main.js`

`main.js` must be the composition root: wire Engine, Input, PostFX, ParticleManager, CameraShake, HitStop, Shockwave, MotionTrail, FloatingText, AudioEngine, GlassHUD, and own full teardown/dispose. Also create or reconcile root `index.html` because `vite.config.js` currently lists it as a build entry.

## 1. Core Gameplay — Mathematical Modeling

**Coordinate system.** World units = meters. Playfield is a 2D plane at `y ∈ [-1.2, 1.2]` (x = lateral, y = vertical), `z = 0` plane. Camera at `(0, 0, 14)` looking at origin, FOV 50°. All gameplay math is 2D (x, y); z is presentation-only (parallax, depth staging).

**Player ship.**
- Position `p = (x, 0)`, `x ∈ [-X_MAX, X_MAX]`, `X_MAX = 7.0`.
- Velocity: `v = inputAxis * PLAYER_SPEED` (14 u/s), with exponential smoothing: `v += (targetV - v) * (1 - e^(-dt/τ))`, `τ = 0.05s` → snappy but no teleport.
- Ship mesh: procedural low-poly fighter (extruded hull + swept wings + emissive cockpit + twin engine nozzles), built from `BufferGeometry` vertex arrays.

**Invader formation (the classic 11×5 grid).**
- Grid: `COLS = 11`, `ROWS = 5`, `55` invaders. Spacing `DX = 1.15`, `DY = 0.95`.
- Formation anchor `A = (ax, ay)`. Each invader `i` at `A + (col_i * DX - 5*DX, row_i * DY - 2*DY) + wobble_i(t)`.
- **Marching:** `ax += dir * marchSpeed * dt`. `marchSpeed = BASE(1.2) * (1 + 0.9 * (1 - alive/55))` — accelerates as the formation thins (classic pressure curve).
- **Edge turn:** if `max|invaderX| > 7.4` → `dir *= -1`, `ay -= DROP(0.55)`.
- **Wobble (retro-futurist upgrade):** each invader gets `wobble_i(t) = sin(t * ω + phase_i) * 0.06` on x, `phase_i = (col_i + row_i) * 0.7` → the whole formation "breathes" like a living swarm.
- **Three species** (top 2 rows = squid, mid 2 = crab, bottom 1 = octopus), each a distinct procedural geometry + PBR material + point-light color.

**Invader fire (stochastic, weighted).**
- Per-frame probability: `P = FIRE_RATE * dt`, `FIRE_RATE = 0.9 + 0.8 * wave` (shots/s).
- Shooter selection: bottom-most alive invader per column, weighted random (bottom rows fire more).
- Bullet: `v = (0, -BULLET_SPEED)`, `BULLET_SPEED = 9 + wave * 0.5` u/s.

**Player fire.**
- Cooldown `COOLDOWN = 0.38s`; max 1 active player bullet (classic) — pool size 2 for headroom.
- Bullet: `v = (0, +16)` u/s.

**Collision (hand-written, no physics lib).**
- All entities are AABBs in (x, y). Test: `|a.x - b.x| < (a.hx + b.hx) && |a.y - b.y| < (a.hy + b.hy)`.
- Player bullet vs invader: on hit → invader dies, score += species value, VFX cascade.
- Invader bullet vs player: on hit → lose life, respawn, brief invulnerability (1.2s, blink).
- Invader vs player (formation reaches ship line): game over.
- Invader vs shield: erodes shield blocks (see §4).

**Scoring (classic values).**
- Squid = 30, Crab = 20, Octopus = 10.
- **Bonus:** first kill of a wave's bottom row = 50 bonus (classic "mystery" bonus, made explicit).
- **Combo:** consecutive kills without being hit → ×1.0, ×1.1, ×1.2… capped ×2.0. Resets on hit.
- **High score:** `localStorage` (no external files).

**Waves / progression.**
- Wave `n`: `marchSpeed *= (1 + 0.12n)`, `FIRE_RATE += 0.3n`, `BULLET_SPEED += 0.5n`, invader count stays 55 (classic) but species mix shifts (more squid = higher value).
- **UFO (mystery ship):** spawns every `15–25s`, traverses top of screen at `v = 12` u/s, worth 50/100/150/300 (random). Adds tension + reward.

**Lives.** 3. Game over → overlay → restart (full state reset, no memory leak).

**Mission**
Build a Vite + vanilla JS + ES Modules Three.js arcade with 14 retro games, starting with `Space_Invaders/`. Strict constraints:
- No external game engines/physics libs; hand-written collision/physics.

Space Invaders is complete and verified. Here's what was done this session:

## Implementation
All 16 `Space_Invaders/` files are in place and mutually consistent:
- **config.js** — single source of truth (species, wave curves, formation grid, palette)
- **entities/** — Player, Invader (shared species geometry), PlayerBullet, InvaderBullet, UFO, Shield (InstancedMesh bunkers)
- **systems/** — Formation (march/drop/edge-turn), Spawner (stochastic fire + UFO), Collision (hand-written AABB), Scoring (combo + localStorage high score), WaveManager (scaling curves)
- **vfx/** — VFXDirector (event→VFX recipes), Starfield (procedural points + nebula)
- **main.js** — composition root wiring Engine, PostFX (bloom), all VFX, HUD, state machine, and full `dispose()`
- **index.html** — game entry

Plus the root **hub `index.html`** (glassmorphism arcade landing page) and a reconciled **`vite.config.js`** (only entries that exist on disk).

## Bugs found & fixed
- **Spawner** duplicated wave-scaling curves → now routes through WaveManager (single source of truth)
- **Player** missing `invulnerable` getter that Collision reads → added
- **Engine** `onResize` captured at construction → mutable hook holder
- **Bullet pools** had no reset → re-acquired bullets lingered at old position for a frame → added `kill()`/`deactivate()` on acquire
- **Bullet trail** drew a connecting line when the tracked bullet changed → reset on target switch
- **Double `shake.update`** per frame (once in VFXDirector, once in main) → trauma decayed at 2× speed → removed the duplicate

## Verified (not just built)
- `npm run build` — 48 modules, both entries emitted, no errors
- **Headless Chromium smoke test** (real page load, SwiftShader WebGL): boots, renders, HUD mounts, Start works, score advances to 30 (one squid kill), **zero console/page errors**
- **Extended test**: 30s of continuous play, lives stay in [0,3], `dispose()` runs clean and removes the HUD
- **Invader-fire test**: player held stationary → lives dropped 3→1, game-over triggered, no page errors

All core gameplay paths (player fire→kill→score, invader fire→player hit→lives→game over, VFX, audio, teardown) are confirmed working in a real browser.
